---
name: video-suggestions
description: Use when the user asks for today's video suggestion, what to post next, or which source videos are already covered on their Mental Empire Studio channels. Also use when asked to scrape their owned publishing channels and linked source channels with yt-dlp to compare uploads against sources.
---

# Video suggestions

Scrape every owned publishing channel and its linked source channels, then pick per channel
the newest source video that has not been covered yet — using the app's own fuzzy matcher.

## Workflow

1. Scrape (writes JSON files + a manifest to a workdir):

   ```
   python .claude/skills/video-suggestions/scripts/scrape_channels.py --workdir <dir> [--only <name-or-handle>]
   ```

   Reads channel/source mappings from the live DB (same discovery rules as the
   channel-source-mapping skill: live profile is `%APPDATA%\Mental Empire Studio`, the
   lowercase `mental-empire-studio` dir is a stale legacy copy). Dead/terminated channels are
   recorded in the manifest with their error and skipped — a terminated source is a finding
   to report, not a crash.

2. Compute suggestions:

   ```
   node .claude/skills/video-suggestions/scripts/compute_suggestions.mjs --workdir <dir>
   ```

   Bundles `shared/match.ts` fresh with the repo's esbuild, so the matching is literally the
   app's own algorithm (`matchUploads`, thresholds 0.82 high / 0.6 floor). Writes
   `<workdir>/suggestions.json` and prints a per-channel summary: today's suggestion
   (newest uncovered), popular alternative (most-viewed uncovered), and the next 5.

3. Report to the user: per channel — suggested video with link, views, length; note channels
   with no linked source; note dead sources. Offer to download the suggested videos as MP3
   (see the mp3-downloads skill).

## Rules that matter

- **Never write a second matcher.** A source video is "covered" when the app's
  `matchUploads` matches it against the uploads of **any** owned channel (videos can be
  live on several channels; cross-posted content must not be re-suggested). The app's own
  code comment warns that a second matcher with a second threshold diverges from the truth.
- **Recency = playlist position.** A flat `/videos` dump is newest-first; entries carry no
  upload dates. Rank 0 is the newest.
- A channel can have several linked source rows (and two rows can be the same YouTube
  channel — see channel-source-mapping). Suggestions dedupe by video id across a channel's
  sources.
- `--only` takes a case-insensitive substring of a channel or source name/handle to scrape
  a single pair quickly.

## Gotchas

- The flat dump omits per-video upload dates; view counts are present but approximate for
  very fresh videos.

- Requires the repo's vendored `resources/bin/yt-dlp.exe` (`npm run fetch:bin` if missing)

input.content:
"""Scrape Mental Empire Studio owned channels + their linked sources (flat yt-dlp JSON).

Writes <workdir>/owned-<n>-<safe>.json, <workdir>/source-<n>-<safe>.json and a manifest.json
describing every channel, its sources, and scrape errors (dead channels are recorded, not
fatal). Read-only against the app DB.
"""

import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

LIVE_DIR = "Mental Empire Studio"
LEGACY_DIR = "mental-empire-studio"
DB_NAME = "mental-empire.db"


def find_db(explicit):
    if explicit:
        p = Path(explicit)
        if not p.exists():
            sys.exit(f"error: --db path does not exist: {p}")
        return p
    appdata = os.environ.get("APPDATA")
    if not appdata:
        sys.exit("error: APPDATA is unset; pass --db explicitly.")
    live = Path(appdata) / LIVE_DIR / DB_NAME
    legacy = Path(appdata) / LEGACY_DIR / DB_NAME
    if live.exists():
        if legacy.exists():
            print(f"note: legacy profile also exists (ignoring it): {legacy}")
        return live
    if legacy.exists():
        print("warning: live profile not found; using LEGACY profile (verify this is intended)")
        return legacy
    sys.exit(f"error: no {DB_NAME} under {appdata}\\{LIVE_DIR} or {appdata}\\{LEGACY_DIR}")


def repo_root():
    # .claude/skills/video-suggestions/scripts/scrape_channels.py -> repo root
    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]
    if not (root / "resources" / "bin" / "yt-dlp.exe").exists():
        sys.exit(f"error: vendored yt-dlp not found under {root}\\resources\\bin (run npm run fetch:bin)")
    return root


def safe_name(s):
    return re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "-", (s or "chan").strip()).strip("-")[:40]


def videos_url(handle, url):
    """Prefer the handle; normalize to the /videos tab (newest-first listing)."""
    if handle and handle.startswith("@"):
        return f"https://www.youtube.com/{handle}/videos"
    if url:
        u = url.rstrip("/")
        return u if u.endswith("/videos") else u + "/videos"
    return None


def scrape(ytdlp, url):
    """Return (entries, channel_meta, None) or (None, None, error)."""
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(
            [str(ytdlp), "--flat-playlist", "-J", "--no-warnings", url],
            capture_output=True, timeout=300,
        )
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        return None, None, "timeout after 300s"
    if r.returncode != 0:
        first = (r.stderr or b"").decode("utf-8", "replace").strip().splitlines()
        return None, None, first[-1][:200] if first else f"exit {r.returncode}"
    try:
        data = json.loads(r.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace"))
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        return None, None, f"bad JSON: {e}"
    entries = data.get("entries") or []
    return entries, data, None


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("--db", help="app DB path (default: auto-discover live profile)")
    ap.add_argument("--workdir", required=True, help="output directory for JSONs + manifest")
    ap.add_argument("--only", help="case-insensitive substring of channel/source name or handle")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    root = repo_root()
    ytdlp = root / "resources" / "bin" / "yt-dlp.exe"
    workdir = Path(a.workdir)
    workdir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    import sqlite3
    con = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{find_db(a.db)}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    cur = con.cursor()

    channels = cur.execute(
        "SELECT id, name, handle, linkedSourceId FROM my_channels ORDER BY name"
    ).fetchall()
    sources = cur.execute(
        "SELECT id, url, handle, name FROM source_channels"
    ).fetchall()
    by_sid = {s[0]: s for s in sources}

    def linked_source_rows(cid, cached_sid):
        ids = {r[0] for r in cur.execute(
            "SELECT id FROM source_channels WHERE linkedMyChannelId=?", (cid,))}
        if cached_sid:
            ids.add(cached_sid)
        return [by_sid[i] for i in sorted(ids) if i in by_sid]

    only = a.only.lower() if a.only else None
    manifest = {
        "generatedAt": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec="seconds"),
        "repo": str(root),
        "owned": [],
    }
    seen_source_rows = {}
    n = 0
    for cid, name, handle, cached_sid in channels:
        srcs = linked_source_rows(cid, cached_sid)
        if only and not any(only in (x or "").lower() for x in
                            [name, handle] + [s[2] or s[3] for s in srcs]):
            continue
        n += 1
        ch_entry = {"id": cid, "name": name, "handle": handle, "file": None,
                    "error": None, "sources": []}
        f = workdir / f"owned-{n}-{safe_name(name)}.json"
        entries, meta, err = scrape(ytdlp, videos_url(handle, None))
        if err:
            ch_entry["error"] = err
            print(f"  OWNED  {name}: FAILED — {err}")
        else:
            f.write_text(json.dumps(meta, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
            ch_entry["file"] = f.name
            print(f"  OWNED  {name}: {len(entries)} uploads")
        for sid, surl, shandle, sname in srcs:
            sf = workdir / f"source-{n}-{safe_name(shandle or sname)}.json"
            sentries, smeta, serr = scrape(ytdlp, videos_url(shandle, surl))
            src_entry = {"rowId": sid, "handle": shandle, "name": sname, "file": None, "error": None}
            if sid in seen_source_rows:
                # already scraped this row for another channel: reuse, don't re-hit YouTube
                prev = seen_source_rows[sid]
                src_entry.update({k: prev[k] for k in ("file", "error")})
                ch_entry["sources"].append(src_entry)
                continue
            if serr:
                src_entry["error"] = serr
                print(f"  SOURCE {shandle or sname}: FAILED — {serr}")
            else:
                sf.write_text(json.dumps(smeta, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
                src_entry["file"] = sf.name
                print(f"  SOURCE {shandle or sname}: {len(sentries)} videos")
            seen_source_rows[sid] = src_entry
            ch_entry["sources"].append(src_entry)
        manifest["owned"].append(ch_entry)
    con.close()

    (workdir / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"\nmanifest: {workdir / 'manifest.json'}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

A naive `yt-dlp -x --audio-format mp3 <url>` fails on this machine in two stages:

1. Default client (`android vr`) resolves a format, then the CDN returns
   **HTTP 403 Forbidden** on the media itself.
2. Forcing `web`/`ios` returns only storyboard formats (PO-token enforcement), or
   "Requested format is not available" / "The page needs to be reloaded".

The working combination — same one the app's downloader falls back to
(`electron/services/downloader.ts`, `GVS_CLIENT_FALLBACKS`):

- `--extractor-args youtube:player_client=web_embedded` (next best: `tv_embedded`)
- `--js-runtimes node` — yt-dlp uses the system Node to solve JS challenges; without it
  even a resolved format 403s
- `-f "bestaudio[ext=m4a]/bestaudio/best"` — the app's `AUDIO_ONLY_FORMAT`
- vendored `resources/bin/ffmpeg.exe` via `--ffmpeg-location`

## Usage

```
python .claude/skills/mp3-downloads/scripts/download_mp3.py <video-url-or-id> --out <dir> [--quality 192] [--client web_embedded]
```

The script tries the client ladder (`web_embedded`, then `tv_embedded`), verifies a real
MP3 landed in `--out`, and prints the final path. Use one output folder per owned channel
(the session convention): `D:\MentalEmpire-MP3\<ChannelName>\`.

## Notes

- Re-downloading a video already on disk: just copy the existing MP3 — same bytes, no
  YouTube hit. Check the folder first.
- The app itself (`npm run dev` → Download screen) uses the same binaries; if in-app
  downloads fail while this script works, compare the player-client ladder.
- Requires `resources/bin/yt-dlp.exe` + `ffmpeg.exe` (`npm run fetch:bin`) and Node on PATH
  (for `--js-runtimes node`).

"""Download a YouTube video's audio as MP3 with the repo's vendored yt-dlp/ffmpeg.

Uses the player-client recipe that works against current YouTube on this machine
(see the mp3-downloads SKILL.md for the 403 background): web_embedded first, then
tv_embedded, always with --js-runtimes node so yt-dlp can solve JS challenges.

  python download_mp3.py <video-url-or-id> --out <dir> [--quality 192] [--client NAME]
"""

import argparse
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

CLIENT_LADDER = ["web_embedded", "tv_embedded"]
AUDIO_FORMAT = "bestaudio[ext=m4a]/bestaudio/best"


def repo_root():
    # .claude/skills/mp3-downloads/scripts/download_mp3.py -> repo root
    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[4]
    if not (root / "resources" / "bin" / "yt-dlp.exe").exists():
        sys.exit(f"error: vendored yt-dlp not found under {root}\\resources\\bin (run npm run fetch:bin)")
    if not (root / "resources" / "bin" / "ffmpeg.exe").exists():
        sys.exit(f"error: vendored ffmpeg not found under {root}\\resources\\bin")
    return root


def normalize_video(v):
    """Accept a watch URL, a bare 11-char id, or anything containing v=<id>."""
    m = re.search(r"[?&]v=([A-Za-z0-9_-]{11})", v)
    if m:
        return f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={m.group(1)}"
    if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z0-9_-]{11}", v):
        return f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={v}"
    if v.startswith("http"):
        return v
    sys.exit(f"error: cannot parse video id/url from: {v}")


def newest_mp3(out_dir, since):
    files = [p for p in Path(out_dir).glob("*.mp3") if p.stat().st_mtime >= since - 2]
    return max(files, key=lambda p: p.stat().st_mtime, default=None)


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    ap.add_argument("video", help="YouTube watch URL or 11-char video id")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="output directory (created if missing)")
    ap.add_argument("--quality", default="192", help="audio bitrate in K (default 192)")
    ap.add_argument("--client", help="force a single youtube player client (skips the ladder)")
    ap.add_argument("--repo", help="repo root (default: auto-detect from script location)")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    root = repo_root() if not a.repo else Path(a.repo)
    ytdlp = root / "resources" / "bin" / "yt-dlp.exe"
    ffmpeg = root / "resources" / "bin" / "ffmpeg.exe"
    out = Path(a.out)
    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    url = normalize_video(a.video)

    ladder = [a.client] if a.client else CLIENT_LADDER
    started = time.time()
    for client in ladder:
        args = [
            str(ytdlp), "-f", AUDIO_FORMAT, "-x", "--audio-format", "mp3",
            "--audio-quality", f"{a.quality}K", "--js-runtimes", "node",
            "--continue", "--no-warnings", "--no-progress",
            "--socket-timeout", "30", "--retries", "3",
            "--ffmpeg-location", str(ffmpeg),
            "--extractor-args", f"youtube:player_client={client}",
            "-o", str(out / "%(title)s.%(ext)s"),
            "--no-playlist", url,
        ]
        print(f"trying player_client={client} ...")
        r = subprocess.run(args, capture_output=True)
        if r.returncode == 0:
            f = newest_mp3(out, started)
            if f is None:
                sys.exit("error: yt-dlp exited 0 but no new .mp3 appeared in --out")
            mb = f.stat().st_size / 1e6
            print(f"OK [{client}] {mb:.1f} MB\n{f}")
            return
        err = (r.stderr or b"").decode("utf-8", "replace").strip().splitlines()
        print(f"  failed: {err[-1][:180] if err else r.returncode}")
    sys.exit("error: every player client in the ladder failed")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
